rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Midian was a people descended from Abraham's son Midian, centered around the Red Sea region and the city built by Midian.
rows.anchor: Medyen Hazret-i İbrâhim evladından Medyen’in nesli bir kavim olup merkezleri Şab denizi havâlisinde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuaib was among Midian's nobility, son of Mekil, son of Yashjur, son of Midian; his gracious address to his people earned him the title Orator of the Prophets.
rows.anchor: Şuayb aleyhisselâm da bu kavmin eşrâfından Şuayb b. Mekil b. Yeşcür b. Medyen’dir. Ve kavmine hüsn-i müracaatından dolayı “Hatîbü’l-enbiyâ” lakabıyla mâruftur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As mentioned in Sura al-Qasas, Moses served Shuaib and became his son-in-law.
rows.anchor: hizmet etmiş ve damadı olmuştu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Careful attention to Shuaib's story reveals points closely relevant to the general morality of contemporary civilizations.
rows.anchor: yakından temas eden noktalar görülür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Like every prophet, Shuaib begins his address by commanding monotheistic worship.
rows.anchor: Müşârün ileyh de her peygamber gibi tevhid emriyle başlayarak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition on short measure and weight shows that trade was Midian's most important occupation.
rows.anchor: bundan anlaşılır ki Medyen kavminin en mühim işleri ticaret imiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being seen in good means enjoying blessing and prosperity; the people have ample means and conduct trade, which is itself a good activity.
rows.anchor: yani bir nimet içinde bulunuyorsunuz, vüs‘atiniz var, alışveriş ediyorsunuz, bu hayırlı bir iştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prosperity calls for protecting people's rights, serving the common good, and thanking God, not acting unjustly; they must not ruin their blessings by cheating measures.
rows.anchor: Bunun muktezâsı haksızlık etmek değil, nâsın hukūkunu gözetip menfa‘at-i âmmeye hizmet ederek Allah’a şükretmektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they persist in injustice through short measure and weight, a day will come whose punishment encompasses everyone, and none will escape; their present good will also be lost.
rows.anchor: bir gün gelecek ki azâbı hepinizi kuşatacak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuaib gives this counsel because he fears for and feels compassion toward his people facing universal punishment.
rows.anchor: Sizin böyle umûmî bir azaba giriftâr olmanızdan korktuğum, size acıdığım için bu nasihatleri yapıyorum

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuaib urges them to give full measure and weight with justice, wrong no one's goods, and avoid causing corruption on earth.
rows.anchor: Ey kavmim kileyi, teraziyi dengi dengine tam tutun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These admonitions also display the people's inward and outward political ethics.
rows.anchor: bu fıkralarda nasihatler dâhilî ve hâricî

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sura al-A'raf further clarifies the point by describing threats along every path, obstructing believers from God's way, and seeking to make it crooked.
rows.anchor: وَلَا تَقْعُدُوا۟ بِكُلِّ صِرَٰطٍۢ تُوعِدُونَ وَتَصُدُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ مَنْ ءَامَنَ بِهِۦ وَتَبْغُونَهَا عِوَجًۭا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root forms ʿathā, ʿathiya, and ʿathayān encompass every kind of religious or worldly corruption and upheaval.
rows.anchor: عثو عثى عثيان dînî dünyevî her nevi fesad ve ihtilâle şâmildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding “as corrupters” excludes actions that outwardly damage something but are truly undertaken for its repair, such as Khidr's acts concerning the boat and boy.
rows.anchor: “müfsidîn” diye hâl ile takyid edilmesi, Hızır’ın gemiyi delmesi, oğlanı öldürmesi gibi cidden ıslah için yapılan harekâtı ihrâc etmek fâidesini müfîddir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The counsel anticipates an objection that observing justice and rectitude in trade and politics would prevent people from earning much.
rows.anchor: Öyle amma ticaret ve siyasette biz böyle adl ü hak ve salâh ile muhayyed olacak olursak fazla bir şey kazanamayız derseniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuaib prayed frequently and was known for this practice.
rows.anchor: Şuayb aleyhisselâm çok namaz kılardı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer, the pillar of religion, is burdensome except for the humble, as the verse in al-Baqara states.
rows.anchor: medlûlünce hâşi‘înden mâ‘adâsının pek ağırına gelen

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those unable to grasp the joy and sublimity of standing and prostrating before God regard prayer as a futile, useless burden.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın huzûrunda divan durmanın, secdelere kapanmanın zevk ve ulviyetini idrak edemeyenlere beyhûde, fâidesiz bir külfetten ibaret görünen büyük bir amel

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mocking those who pray is characteristic of disbelief and of rebellious unbelievers.
rows.anchor: namaz kılanlarla eğlenmek küfrün muktezâsı ve azgın kâfirlerin mu‘tâdıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By attributing his teaching to prayer, they reject Shuaib's monotheistic, legal, and ethical message, attack his reason and discernment, and mock his prophethood.
rows.anchor: bunları bilhassa onun namazına isnad ederek akl ü rüşdüne taarruz ve nübüvvetiyle istihzâ ediyorlar

words: أَوْ أَن نَّفْعَلَ فِىٓ أَمْوَٰلِنَا مَا نَشَٰٓؤُا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They regard worshipping only God and respecting justice in trade and politics as foolish restrictions on freedom.
rows.anchor: Yalnız Allah’a ibadet edip türlü türlü mâbudlara kul olmaktan kurtulmayı

words: أَوْ أَن نَّفْعَلَ فِىٓ أَمْوَٰلِنَا مَا نَشَٰٓؤُا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuaib did not prohibit people from disposing of their own wealth as they wished; he prohibited wronging other people's property, thereby affirming rather than curtailing freedom.
rows.anchor: Şuayb aleyhisselâm onlara “mallarınızda istediğiniz gibi tasarruf etmeyin” dememişti, “nâsın eşyâsına haksızlık yapmayın” demişti. Bu ise hürriyeti men‘değil, tesbit ve teyit oluyordu

words: أَوْ أَن نَّفْعَلَ فِىٓ أَمْوَٰلِنَا مَا نَشَٰٓؤُا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unless everyone's property and rights are protected, no one can feel secure in their rights or freely manage their own wealth.
rows.anchor: herkesin emvâli ve hukūku mahfuz olmadıkça kimse hakkından emin olamaz, emvâlinde dilediği gibi tasarruf yapamaz

words: أَوْ أَن نَّفْعَلَ فِىٓ أَمْوَٰلِنَا مَا نَشَٰٓؤُا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people treat others' wealth as their own and seek to exploit whatever their power permits, presenting the demand for justice as a constraint on their liberty.
rows.anchor: onlar nâsın mallarını kendi malları imiş gibi farz ediyorlar, güçlerinin yetebildiği tecavüzü yapmak istiyorlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their question is sophistry and taunting: they sarcastically call him sensible while pretending that prayer tells them to abandon ancestral worship and unrestricted exploitation.
rows.anchor: “emvâlimizde dilediğimizi yapmaktan vazgeçmemizi namazın mı emrediyor, sofu sen ne akıllısın be!” gibi mugālata ile târiz ve istihzâya kalkışıyorlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idolatry, arrogant contempt for prayer, and sophistry that invokes liberty and trade to excuse fraud, aggression, insolence, and corruption recur among modern unbelievers; contemporary people should heed Shuaib and Midian.
rows.anchor: medeniyet-i hâzıra insanları kıssa-i Şuayb ve Medyen’i pek ziyade nazar-ı ibret ile dinlemelidirler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Have you considered?” means “Have you seen your condition? If so, tell me what you say.”
rows.anchor: gördünüz mü hâlinizi yani gördünüzse söyleyin bakayım

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuaib's clear proof from his Lord is decisive evidence; if he speaks through knowledge and prophethood, how could he oppose his Lord's revelation and explanation?
rows.anchor: Rabbim Hak teâlâ’dan kat‘î ve açık bir burhan üzerinde bulunuyor, söylediklerimi ilm ü nübüvvetle söylüyorsam ne dersiniz? Ben Rabbimin vahy ü beyânına muhalefet edebilir miyim?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good provision is bestowed from God's treasury, not earned by Shuaib himself; it includes lawful material wealth and the spiritual gifts of prophethood and wisdom, means of eternal life.
rows.anchor: hazîne-i kereminden beni maddeten mânen güzel bir surette merzuk etmiş, hem helâlinden mal hem de ebedî hayatın medârı olan nübüvvet ve hikmet nasip eylemiştir

words: وَمَآ أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُخَالِفَكُمْ إِلَىٰ مَآ أَنْهَىٰكُمْ عَنْهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuaib does not forbid them shirk, violating people's rights, and corruption in order to do those things himself; his advice to adopt monotheism and justice is not a scheme to seize their freedom and reserve the forbidden conduct for himself.
rows.anchor: murâdım, gāye-i maksadım hürriyetinizi alıp sizi çevirip de o menhiyyâtı münhasıran kendim yapmak değildir

words: وَمَآ أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُخَالِفَكُمْ إِلَىٰ مَآ أَنْهَىٰكُمْ عَنْهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He is not plotting tyranny or monopoly so that they avoid sin, cheating, and consuming people's property while he does those things and claims pleasure for himself.
rows.anchor: Allah’a karşı siz günaha girmeyin de ben gireyim, siz aldatmayın da ben aldatayım, halkın emvâlini siz yemeyin de ben yiyeyim

words: إِنْ أُرِيدُ إِلَّا ٱلْإِصْلَٰحَ مَا ٱسْتَطَعْتُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His sole aim is to bring about reform as far as he is able.
rows.anchor: Muradım başka değil, gücüm yettikçe ıslahtan ibarettir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His success comes only through God's guidance and grace.
rows.anchor: Muvaffakiyetim de ancak Allah iledir. Allah’ın hidâyet ve inâyetiyledir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuaib relies on God alone.
rows.anchor: Ancak O’na tevekkül ettim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To turn in repentance means repeatedly returning to God, seeking His protection, and submitting to Him.
rows.anchor: döner döner O’na dönerim, O’na dehâlet eder, O’na teslim olurum

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shiqaq here is hostility, discord, and opposition to Shuaib; he warns that it could bring them a calamity like those that struck the peoples of Noah, Hud, and Salih.
rows.anchor: sakının bana şikāk u adâvet ve zıddiyet sizi Nûh kavminin veya Hûd kavminin veya Sâlih kavminin başına gelen gibi bir musibet ile tecrim etmesin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot's people are near in time and place, or the Midianites are near them in disbelief and corruption.
rows.anchor: daha Lût kavmi sizden uzak değil yakın zamandadır. Veya zaman ve mekânda olduğu gibi küfr ü fesad itibariyle de siz onlara yakınsınız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This refrain recalls the ending of Lot's account and warns the people by echoing it.
rows.anchor: Görülüyor ki bu fâsıla kavm-i Lût kıssasının âhirindeki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They should seek forgiveness and then repent by returning to God; however many their sins, abandoning them and repenting brings God's mercy and love.
rows.anchor: günahlarınız ne kadar çok olursa olsun vazgeçer istiğfar ve tevbe ederseniz rahmet ve mahabbetine nâil olursunuz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is exceedingly merciful and loving.
rows.anchor: O benim Rabbim çok merhametli, çok sevgilidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One valid sense is that the call to truth—to the true deity and true religion—is a call to God alone; calls and propaganda made in another's name are false.
rows.anchor: Hakka davet, insanları hak mâbuda, hak dine davet ancak O’na olan davettir. Allah’tan başkası nâmına yapılan davetler, propagandalar hep bâtıldır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another valid sense is true supplication: prayer that is properly directed and answered belongs to invocation and worship of God alone.
rows.anchor: hak dua, yani yerine masruf olan ve icâbet görecek olan dua, ancak Allah’a olan dua ve ibadettir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third valid sense is the call to the true object sought: God alone first and directly shows and guides to truth.
rows.anchor: hak matlûba davet, evvelen ve bizzat hakkı gösterip hidâyet edecek olan O’dur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that God guides to truth is supported by Yunus 10:35; truth cannot be invited to without reliance on God's disclosure and guidance.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın beyan ve irşâdına istinad etmeksizin hakka davet olunamaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The invoked include deities promoted in their name, beings from whom needs are requested, and those called upon for aid or supplicated.
rows.anchor: o kâfirlerin Allah’tan başka davet ettikleri veya dua edip durdukları yani namlarına propaganda yaptıkları, hâcet diledikleri mâbudlar, imdâda çağırdıkları

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those invoked cannot answer with anything or fulfill any request by their own power.
rows.anchor: onlara hiçbir şeyle icâbet edemezler hiçbir dileklerini kendiliklerinden yerine getiremezler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The futile invocation resembles a thirsty person reaching both hands toward distant water, which cannot come into his mouth by itself.
rows.anchor: ancak ağzına erişsin diye suya doğru iki avucunu açan susuz gibi boşuna avuç açmış olurlar

words: وَمَا دُعَآءُ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ إِلَّا فِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayers of unbelievers are wholly misguided.
rows.anchor: kâfirlerin duası da sırf dalâldedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is obvious that inanimate idols cannot answer any prayer.
rows.anchor: putların da hiçbir duaya cevap veremiyecekleri âşikârdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the relative pronoun alladhina ordinarily denotes rational beings, restricting the referent to idols alone contradicts the apparent wording; rational beings worshipped beside God are included too.
rows.anchor: وَٱلَّذِينَ mevsûlü zevi’l-ukūlde zâhir olduğu cihetle bunu yalnız asnâm ile tevil etmek hilâf-ı zâhirdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even rational beings made into objects of worship and supplication cannot answer any prayer, just like idols.
rows.anchor: yalnız şuursuz putlar değil, Allah’ın mâdûnunda mâbud ittihaz edilen, yalvarılan zevi’l-ukūlün de putlar gibi hiçbir duaya icâbet edemeyecekleri

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording seems puzzling for public cries, since people can hear them and sometimes respond in part.
rows.anchor: duyduğu ve kısmen olsun icâbet de edebildiği dermeyan olunur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Limiting prayer to hidden, inward supplication would remove the objection, but the text gives no clue for that restriction and its monotheistic context weighs against it.
rows.anchor: bu tahsis veya takyîde başkaca bir karîne olmadığı gibi, âyetin tevhîde müte‘allik olan siyâk u mezâkı da buna muhaliftir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deeper truth is that no one can answer a supplication independently of God; all efficacy and connection among distinct beings depends on the One who governs them.
rows.anchor: hakikatte Allah’tan kat‘-ı nazarla hiç kimsenin duaya icâbet etmesine imkân olmadığı anlatılmıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Distinct individual entities are separate precisely because each is its own thing; none is present in another, and they do not possess or interpenetrate one another's selfhood.
rows.anchor: ve her biri diğer bir ayn olan mütemâyiz şeylerin yekdiğerine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The possibility that separate things affect and communicate with one another is a profound philosophical problem, including how matter affects matter, soul affects body, and body affects soul.
rows.anchor: meselesi feylesofları hayrette bırakan en mu‘dil mes’ele-i felsefiye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only by recourse to divine unity can interaction be explained; without the supreme One, the world would be disconnected things unable to relate to one another.
rows.anchor: Şimşekler çakmaz, bulutlar inşâ edilmez, yağmurlar yağmaz, yıldırımlar düşmezdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Natural processes and communication, from clouds, rain, and lightning to Zayd's cry reaching Amr, occur through the Lord of the worlds' command and management.
rows.anchor: Bunlar olabiliyorsa hiç şüphe yok ki hep Rabbü’l-âlemîn’in emr ü tedbîriyle oluyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A creature to whom one appeals is separate and distant, unable by itself to convey one's inner feeling or another thing to it, like a thirsty person reaching toward water from afar.
rows.anchor: kendisinden ayrı ve uzaktır. Kendindeki bir hissi, bir şeyi diğerine nakletmesine imkân yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even breathing depends on God's permission; when death comes and the soul is taken by God's command, all the world's physicians cannot restore one breath to the dead.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ’nın izn ü müsaadesi olmayınca insan hava içinde nefes bile alamaz. Nitekim ecel gelip emr-i Rab olan rûh kabz olunduğu zaman, dünyanın tabibleri toplansa ölüye bir nefes veremezler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People and angels can hear cries only by God's permission, and can respond or help only by His leave; without it ears do not hear and hearts do not will.
rows.anchor: Bir insanın feryâd ü ilticâsını diğer insanların veya melâikenin işitebilmesi sem‘ü ibsâra mâlik olan Allah teâlâ’nın emr ü müsaadesi sayesinde olduğu gibi, mümkin olan icâbet ve i‘ânede bulunabilmeleri de öyledir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those besides God are independently unable to answer a needy person's prayer because they are separate from one another and cannot create anything in the first instance.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın mâdûnundakiler nefislerinde birbirlerinden uzak oldukları

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is closer to each person than that person's own self; al-Baqara 2:186 says He is near and answers the supplication of the one who calls.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ, herkese kendinden bile karîbdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears even the most secret prayers, answers them, creates what is not already available to give, and joins separated things through His power and dominion.
rows.anchor: En gizli duaları bile işitir, icâbet eder, vereceği mevcud değilse yaratır, hâlıktır. Birbirinden ayrı olan şeyleri kudretiyle, melekûtuyla yekdiğerine ulaştırır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can bring a person to water or bring water to the person's mouth; every relation among things is created by His act and command.
rows.anchor: Dilerse insanı suyun yanına götürür, dilerse suyu onun ağzına getirir. Bütün eşyâ beynindeki irtibat ve münasebet hep O’nun halk u emriyledir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here prostration means bowing down and submitting in obedience.
rows.anchor: secde eder boyun eğer, inkıyad eyler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those in the heavens may mean angels, or intellects, spirits, and lofty faculties in the higher realms.
rows.anchor: melâike veya yukarı makamlarda bulunan ukūl u ervâh

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those on earth may mean humanity and jinn, the two weighty species generally, or lower souls.
rows.anchor: yerdeki kimseler yani umûmiyetle ins ü cin, sekaleyn, veya aşağıda bulunan nüfûs-ı sâfile

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All submit whether willingly or unwillingly, voluntarily or under compulsion.
rows.anchor: gerek tav‘an ve gerek kerhen ister istemez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their shadows also prostrate morning and evening; if the people themselves do not submit willingly, their shadows submit under compulsion to God's command, not their owners'.
rows.anchor: gölgeleri de tav‘an değilse kerhen ve bi’l-mecbûriye Allah’a secde ederler. Gölgelerin bile yerlere kapanışı sâhiplerinin değil, Allah’ın emrine inkıyaddır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse may also hint that bodies are like shadows in relation to intellects and spirits, since spirits are luminous while bodies are dark.
rows.anchor: Burada ukūl ü ervâh mukabilinde ebdân ü ecsâmın birer gölge mesâbesinde olduğuna da işaret vardır denebilir. Zira ervâh nûrânî, ecsâm zulmânîdir
